texts.9194e6facaa9: Objective for processing: The National Vascular Registry (NVR) is based on prospectively-collected, patient-level data on patients who have had vascular surgery. The tabulated HES data will show the number of procedures performed at NHS trusts and a national level and will be used by the National Vascular Registry to calculate case-ascertainment for English NHS Trusts and nationally. The Registry was established in 2013 to measure the quality and outcomes of care for patients who undergo major vascular surgery in NHS hospitals. By collecting data from NHS Trusts providing care to patients who have had vascular surgery the Registry is able to provide outcomes on patient characteristics, pre-operative tests, patient fitness prior to surgery, and postoperative outcomes. The National Vascular Registry is run by the Clinical Effectiveness Unit of the Royal College of Surgeons. HES data required for: • Calculating the expected number of cases per NHS Trust and nationally • To identify all eligible NHS Trusts that should be submitting data to the Registry • The expected number of cases will be reported at a national and NHS Trust level in the NVR annual report. This is a publically available report and will highlight whether trusts are submitting the expected number of cases on an annual basis. This will help with the interpretation of the results produced from the NVR data. • The expected number of cases will be reported back to NHS Trusts. NHS Trusts will use these reports to assess whether they are entering the expected number of cases in the NVR and if not they will address this and make improvements in their data submission. • This is a request for quarterly HES data. Providing data on quarterly activity to NHS trusts has proven to be a useful time period in terms of allowing them to check discrepancies between HES and the NVR data. For example, due to the on-going reorganisation of vascular surgery in the UK, a large number of NHS trusts have stopped performing surgery over the last few years. Requesting data by quarter allows the Registry to confirm the time period during which trusts have stopped performing vascular surgery and identify those NHS trusts that are eligible to submit data to the NVR. • The calculation of case-ascertainment requires unsuppressed data. The purpose of the tabulated data is to validate the completeness of the cases submitted by NHS trusts to the Registry. Differences between activity levels recorded in HES and the Registry may be less than five – hence precision in small numbers is required. Moreover, if small numbers were suppressed, it would be impossible to calculate case ascertainment rates accurately for all NHS trusts as the true denominator would be unknown. Processing activities: 1. All eligible NHS trusts submit data on their patients who have had vascular surgery to a system hosted by Northgate Information Solutions. This system holds data on patient characteristics, pre-operative tests, patient fitness prior to surgery, operations performed, and postoperative outcomes. The CEU will analyse this data to produce the number of operations carried out by each NHS trust. 2. Tabulated HES data is sent by the HSCIC to the CEU. 3. The CEU then analyse the tabulated HES data to produce expected case ascertainment figures for inclusion in the outputs listed in the next section. The CEU will only use the data for the stated purposes. 4. In the publications produced by the National Vascular Registry, the RCS would ensure that any numbers published would adhere to the small numbers guidance from the Office for National Statistics so that individual patients could not be identified. 5. The requested data will be stored on a restricted data server at the Royal College of Surgeons. Only members of the National Vascular Registry will have access to the tabulated figures. The data server is connected via a centrally-managed Windows Active Directory network, physically connected via Enterasys N7 core switches. The network incorporates Network Access Control and Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems. There is a Cisco PIX 515 Firewall configured to restrict port access to known services only, VLAN segregation of all network traffic, and monthly vulnerability scans of externally facing services. The server rooms in the College are physically protected by manual keypad locks and CCTV. Specific outputs expected, including target date: As well as the results being published in the annual Reports of the Audit, these results will also be presented at professional medical conferences. Results from supplementary analysis will be published in appropriate media, such as NVR reports and peer-reviewed journal articles. The main products of the Audit will be the public Annual reports and other scientific publications (peer-review articles, conference presentations). The NVR is commissioned to produce one "State of the Nation" annual report each year and consultant level outcomes. Results will be disseminated at professional conferences and in peer-reviewed journals shortly after publication. Publications related to the Audit methods (eg, a risk-adjustment model) rather than information of clinical practice and outcomes will be published on an ad hoc basis. The National Vascular Registry Annual Report – target delivery date November 2015. The expected case ascertainment figures will be published at NHS Trust level in the Consultant Outcomes Publication as required by NHS England under Everyone Counts. Trust level data completeness reports – on an ongoing , regular basis The Consultant Outcomes are published on the Professional Body website (http://www.vsqip.org.uk/surgeon-outcomes/) and NHS Choices (https://www.nhs.uk/Service-Search/consultants/performanceindicators/1026). The target date for delivery is July 2015. The HES data requested will not be at individual patient level, but may contain small numbers within individual quarters. The RCS will ensure that the outputs are small numbers suppressed in line with the HES small number analysis guide. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: The aim of the National Vascular Registry (NVR0 is to improve the quality of care for patients undergoing vascular procedures by publishing comparative information on the processes and outcomes of care delivered in England and Wales. The Registry is part of the national programme of clinical audits and forms an essential element of the quality improvement initiatives undertaken by the Vascular Society of Great Britain and Ireland (VSGBI). The tabulations of vascular surgery activity from HES underpins CEU’s ability to measure case ascertainment across English NHS trusts. Knowledge of case-ascertainment has various important benefits. First, it aids the interpretation of the figures published by the NVR – by showing that hospitals have high levels of case-ascertainment, it increases the confidence that patients and surgeons have in the published rates of postoperative mortality and complications. This improves CEU’s ability to demonstrate that vascular services deliver a safe and effective service. NHS trusts not meeting the expected case ascertainment will address their lower than expected submission rate and make improvements and this will in turn benefit patients. The Registry is able to report the following year whether improvements have been made. The trust profiles are publically available, providing transparency and enabling patient choice. Second, each English NHS trust is required to submit data to national clinical audits that cover services that they provide. Providing information on case ascertainment to the NHS trusts helps them to track their participation, make improvements where necessary and quality assure their local processes which will in turn benefit patients. The Registry is able to report back to NHS trusts whether there have been improvements in their data submission. These reports provide transparency on the trusts’ data submission and encourage submission of all eligible records to the NVR.
